newsitem.title: USA: ValuJet given approval to fly again.
newsitem.headline: ValuJet given approval to fly again.

text.p: The Transportation Department gave ValuJet Airlines approval Thursday to resume flying, ending a three-month grounding for safety reasons.

Betty Monroe, spokeswoman for Georgia Republican Michael Collins, said approval was given Thursday afternoon, effective immediately. The approval order was later confirmed by the Transportation Department.
The low-cost carrier was grounded June 17 following a safety inspection of its operations started after its Flight 592 crashed near Florida May 11, killing all 110 people on board.

The Federal Aviation Administration had reached an agreement with ValuJet to ground the low-cost Atlanta-based airline following a year-long inspection that uncovered a series of maintenance and operations failings.

Following remedial action by the carrier, the FAA on Aug. 29 gave ValuJet approval to resume flying, but the Transportation Department held up its approval pending comments by the public and other interested parties.
Monroe said the department told Congressman Collins' office it needed the additional month to fully review every charge made against the carrier. "That's why things got dragged out," she said.
